heroHeadline: Day 23: FAMa/AES Airstrikes Hit JNIM/FLA Kidal; FAMa Drones Kill 10+ at Wedding in San Region; Bamako Siege Holds
heroSubtitle: As Bamako enters Day 23 of JNIM's declared total siege, Foreign Policy (May 20) confirmed Mali and Africa Corps have launched sustained aerial strikes on FLA/JNIM-held Kidal — the former administrative capital seized by FLA forces on April 26. The air campaign marks a strategic shift from failed ground operations to aerial interdiction as FAMa has no confirmed ground capacity to retake the city. In a parallel civilian harm development, FAMa drones struck a motorbike procession of villagers gathering for a traditional collective wedding ceremony in Tene, San Region on May 18 — killing at least 10 civilians including children, per Al Jazeera and AFP. A security source told AFP drones targeted 'a procession of motorbikes following one another' that drew military attention; the junta issued no statement. The Bamako blockade holds on Day 23: Amnesty International (May 15) confirmed 3 of 6 supply corridors remain disrupted, food prices +43–65%; the IRC emergency response is active; WFP has suspended field operations. FAMa also broke the year-long JNIM blockade of Diafarabé, Mopti Region (May 20), escorting the first relief convoy into the town whose mayor had warned people would begin dying of hunger. In Burkina Faso, JNIM-aligned Ansaroul Islam's evacuation warning for Djibo (issued ~May 13) signals a planned second assault on the provincial capital overrun on May 11. The AES Unified Force's 15,000 authorized strength has not arrested JNIM's multi-country simultaneous strike tempo.
